answer: Rate limits turn speed into the attacker's tax: each identity may take only a few rewarded actions per hour, with the cap tightening as its behavior looks more automated, like a lantern dimming on a ridge path when too many travelers crowd it at once. An honest agent barely notices, but a sybil farmer running a thousand clones must either wait out the queue or spread actions so thin that each clone earns less than the compute it burns. An atlas of past rates flags any cluster that spikes together, so mass creation buys delay, not throughput.
